default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-138.title: Choppy-window micro-break fade
E-138.hypothesis: When Kaufman's efficiency ratio over the last 30-60 minutes is low, price is churning between liquidity providers on both sides and nobody initiates; a close beyond the previous three bars' high/low in such a window is a small order pushing through a thin quote, which the market makers fade, so fade it.

E-139.title: Regression-channel dip in a straight trend
E-139.hypothesis: When the closes of the last hour sit on a straight line (high R-squared), one participant is working a steady parent order; a close more than k residual deviations against that line is a short-term liquidity seller (buyer) the parent order absorbs, so buy the dip below a rising line (mirror).

E-140.title: Initial-balance extension level fade
E-140.hypothesis: Market Profile traders project multiples of the initial-balance width (first 30/60 minutes) beyond the IB high/low and scale out there; a bar reaching such an extension from the inside and closing back short of it shows those take-profits absorbing the push, so fade back toward the IB.

E-142.title: Prior-hour close retest hold
E-142.hypothesis: A completed hourly candle that closed strongly (large body for its range) leaves its close as the price where the hour's winners marked their position; a return to that close that holds on the hour's side meets their adds and the late counter-traders are trapped, so trade in the hour's direction.

E-143.title: Vacuum-bar fade
E-143.hypothesis: A bar with a range far above normal for its minute but only normal-or-less volume moved through an empty book (quotes pulled for a moment), not on new information; when quotes refill, liquidity providers lean the price back, so fade the bar's direction.

E-145.title: Channel-midline rotation follow
E-145.hypothesis: After price tags the edge of its recent channel and then closes back through the channel midline, the edge buyers are under water and the rotation traders target the opposite edge; follow the midline cross toward the other side.

E-146.title: Swing-leg stretch fade
E-146.hypothesis: A zigzag swing leg (reversal threshold r) whose length is far above the typical leg of the last 20 sessions has outrun the swing traders' usual targets; once a bar closes against the leg, their profit-taking and the late entrants' exits revert it, so fade the stretched leg.

E-147.title: Quiet-drift fade
E-147.hypothesis: Several consecutive closes in one direction on bars much narrower than normal for their minute is quote shading by liquidity providers in an empty market, not initiative buying; with no committed side behind it the drift reverts, so fade the bar that completes the drift.
